# Task
## Captain's intent
Hackathon {Tech: Europe} Agentic AI Hack Zurich today, live demo 20:00. The iPhone app (frontend/BeaverAgent) currently uses an earlier dark-glass look with a blue accent. The final brand and implementation kit for the product is now in the repo at docs/brand-kit/ (Orbs, v1.0, final ring direction): monochrome, fine-line, calm, compact; no glass blur, no neon glows, no decorative gradients, no large assistant avatars; content stays primary. The app should follow this kit.

## Firstmate spec
- Base origin/develop. Read docs/brand-kit/README.md completely, plus tokens.json and tokens.css; open docs/brand-kit/index.html in headless Chrome to see the intended look. Read the repo AGENTS.md and .entire/graph-agent.md.
- Change Theme.swift values to the kit: light and dark canvas/surface/raised/text/secondary/border colors exactly as in tokens.json, system SF font with the kit's type scale (display 36/40 on mobile, section 28/34, card title 18/24 semibold, body 15/22, control 14/20, metadata 12/16), spacing grid, radii (card 24, control 12, pill full), 1px borders, shadow only on floating surfaces, motion curves and durations from the kit, reduced motion honored. Remove glass materials, blur and gradients; primary button = text color filled, secondary = raised with border; no color-only status (use text plus check or warning icons). Keep existing Theme token names where possible so other screens restyle automatically; if a name must change, update every use in the app.
- Apply the kit's card rules to the existing card and sheet views (context, result, confirmation, done, error; bottom contextual sheet with 16px side margins on mobile; confirmation summarizes exact writes with Confirm primary and Cancel secondary).
- Do NOT touch the orb renderer: another worker ports the thinking-orbs ring into OrbView and frontend/BeaverAgent/BeaverAgent/Orb/ on feature/wp1-thinking-orbs. Other workers also add Dashboard/, Profile/ and NativeCards/ screens; do not edit those folders.
- Do not change the visible product name; leave it as it is on develop.
- Verify: xcodebuild for the iPhone 17 Pro simulator; before/after screenshots of idle, listening, reply with cards, confirmation, settings, in light and dark, under frontend/screenshots/brand/, shown in the PR. Check the kit's demo acceptance checklist items that apply to the app (390pt width no overflow, large text usable, safe areas).
- Entire: confirm entire status shows Enabled before committing; checkpoint refs go to origin with each push.
- Branch feature/wp1-brand-theme from origin/develop, PR against develop, Conventional Commits like feat(ios): ...

   `echo "{state} [at=<epoch>]: {one short line}" >> '/Users/batu/Projects/agentic/firstmate/state/micro-intent-ios-brand-theme-v1.status'`
   States: working, needs-decision, blocked, paused, done, failed.
   Substitute `<epoch>` with the current Unix time in seconds - run `date +%s` and write the number it printed; a stamp that is not plain digits records no time at all.
   Each append wakes firstmate, so report sparingly: only phase changes a supervisor
   would act on (setup done, bug reproduced, fix implemented, validation passed) and the
   needs-decision/blocked/paused/done/failed states. No step-by-step FYI progress lines;
   firstmate reads your pane for that.
   Whenever you mention a PR anywhere - a status line, your terminal, a summary - write its full
   https:// URL exactly as the forge printed it, never a bare number such as "PR 108"; firstmate
   copies that URL from your line rather than assembling one.
   A mid-task `working:` line (including setup complete) is nonterminal: do not end the

   cadence instead of treating it as a possible wedge. Use `blocked:` when you are stuck and need help.
5. If you hit the same obstacle twice, append `blocked [at=<epoch>]: {why}` and stop; firstmate will help.
6. If a decision belongs above the implementation worker (product choices, destructive actions),
   append `needs-decision [at=<epoch>]: {summary of options}` and stop. Firstmate will reply with the decision.

   daemon error is also a real block.
   Only after ruling out socket refusal, if the run is still running or fixing, reattach and keep
   going. A drive-call error, timeout, slow read, or generic unreachability is NOT a daemon error:
   the daemon accepts `respond` immediately and runs the round in the background, so a killed or
